entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A. informs that he has procured complete instructions in the matter including up-to-date case diary and charge sheet in this case has also been submitted.

2. Heard Shri Ajeet Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Munna for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 350 of 2023, under Section 366 and 376 I.P.C., Police Station Atrauli, District Hardoi,
during trial.

4. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case and he has not committed any offence as claimed by the prosecution.

5. It is further submitted that the first information report of the incident has been lodged by the brother of the victim/prosecutrix on 29.06.2023 at Police Station Atrauli, District Hardoi, alleging therein that on 26.06.2023 at about 11:00 am.

his sister aged about 16 years had gone to ease Munna vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118664757/

sentences.text: On being recovered, on 30.06.2023 the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., wherein she has not imputed any allegations against the applicant and has stated that she had left the home of her parents voluntarily, as she had scolded by them and resided at a 'eucalyptus orchard' and had gone to 'Bharawan Chauraha' from where she made a call to the applicant and had gone with him to the home of his sister and remained there for two days and when she was returning, she was apprehended by the police.

6. It is also submitted that in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. on 06.07.2023, the prosecutrix/victim has changed her statement and stated that she had accompanied the applicant to the house of his sister where she was sexually assaulted.

7. Highlighting the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it is vehemently submitted that it is stated by the victim in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that at the time of the incident the whole family of the sister of the applicant were present in the house and the tenor and texture of the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. would reveal that she was a consenting party.

8. It is next submitted that age of the prosecutrix in her statement is stated as 18 years and as per the school leaving certificate of Class-V her date of birth is shown as 08.05.2005 whereby she comes about 18 years and one month and on the basis of ossification test her age has been determined as 18-19 years.
Thus, she was major at the date and time of the incident and as she was a consenting party, no offence in fact has been committed by the applicant.

9. It is further submitted that applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 11.07.2023 and he is not having any criminal history and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

10. Learned A.G.A. on the other hand submits that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail, but could not confront the fact that age of the prosecutrix, as recorded in the school record is 08.05.2005.
11.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that as per the educational credentials the age of the prosecutrix appears to be about more than 18 years at the date and time of the incident.
As per the ossification test, her age has been assessed as 18-19 years and she in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has also stated her age to be of 18 years.
Thus, the prosecutrix/victim at the date and time of the incident appears to be major.

In the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she has not imputed any allegations against the applicant, rather she stated that she had left the home of her parents as she was scolded by them and had made a call to the applicant, who had taken her to the house of his sister.
However, in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. for the very first time allegation of sexual assault has been levelled.

However, it is admitted to the prosecutrix that the applicant was known to him and all the members of the family and his sister were present in the house when the incident had occurred and it is in this background, it is submitted on behalf of the applicant that the allegations, as levelled Munna vs State Of U.P. 2 by the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., has been given under the pressure of her family members and no such incident had occurred and also that she was a 'consenting party'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 11.07.2023 without any criminal antecedents.
Charge sheet in this case has also been submitted and the presence of the applicant may be secured before the trial Court by placing adequate conditions.

12. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.
13.

Let the accused/applicant- Munna involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
14. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
15. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
16. Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
